################################################################################
# CONCLUSION / INTERPRETATION
################################################################################

Scope and safety
----------------
Targeted only /dev/sr0 and /dev/sg3 (SCSI 5:0:0:0, ata6). The shared AHCI
controller/host/bus was not reset because it also carries sda, sdb and sdc.
No WRITE BUFFER, firmware flash, EEPROM/NVRAM write, optical-media write, or
other persistent modification was performed. In this initial unprivileged pass,
device- and target-level reset requests with --no-esc were rejected for lack of
CAP_SYS_ADMIN. The appended root-level addendum supersedes that limitation and
documents the later exact-target reset/reprobe and full libata trace.

Main observations
-----------------
* The transport and command processor remain responsive. INQUIRY, GET
  CONFIGURATION, mode pages, mechanism status, RPC information, GET
  PERFORMANCE and read-only Optiarc vendor-memory queries complete promptly.
  The vendor reads returned coherent identity strings including
  "Sony Optiarc Inc.", "AD-5260S" and firmware "1.00".
* With the tray open, TUR reports 02/3A/02 (medium not present - tray open), so
  the tray state is distinguished correctly. LOAD itself completes GOOD.
* Immediately after LOAD, TUR changes to 02/04/01 (logical unit is in process
  of becoming ready). In the passive high-resolution trace, the SKSV progress
  field advances deterministically from 0x0000 through 0x6CCC (42.499%) over
  about 1.73 s, resets to 0x00DA (0.333%) at about 1.83 s, and reaches the
  terminal 02/30/00 at about 1.95 s.
* During that interval GESN media remains 00 06 04 5e 00 00 00 00: door closed,
  but medium-present is never asserted. GESN device-busy reports status 3
  (Deferred) with a decreasing time estimate, confirming that an internal
  recognition operation is running rather than the host simply waiting.
* Injecting START STOP UNIT (immediate and synchronous), READ(10), and the
  known NEC/Optiarc F3 quality-scan init/interval/read commands during the
  04/01 interval only returns the current becoming-ready sense. The progress
  curve and terminal result remain effectively identical to the passive run.
  The commands are serialized/gated behind the internal recognition state
  machine; none forces spindle operation or bypasses media qualification.
* A synchronous LOAD blocks for 1769.701 ms and returns GOOD, then TUR briefly
  shows 04/01 before the same 30/00 endpoint. This is repeatable firmware-side
  media-recognition logic, not an SG_IO or SATA timeout.
* TUR with 5 s, 15 s and 60 s host command timeouts still returns 02/30/00 in
  roughly 12-19 ms once recognition has failed. Other media-dependent MMC
  commands (profile/TOC/capacity/disc info/DVD structure/sector reads) likewise
  fail immediately with the same 02/30/00. READ FORMAT CAPACITIES returns GOOD
  but only a type-3 descriptor: no recognized medium.
* No host byte, driver transport error, SATA CRC error, libata reset, kernel
  timeout, or matching kernel-journal event was observed. The drive never
  returns the more specific 09/02 FOCUS SERVO FAILURE or 09/03 SPINDLE SERVO
  FAILURE; its firmware collapses the terminal condition to 30/00.

Diagnosis
---------
Software cannot conclusively distinguish focus/pickup/RF failure from a failed
spindle motor/driver/FG path on this firmware. It does, however, localize the
fault below the MMC/media-recognition layer: SATA transport, ATAPI command
processing, the controller MCU, tray sensing and substantial firmware logic
are working. Because the disc physically never rotates and firmware never
asserts medium-present, a failure of focus acquisition/reflection/RF detection
(pickup, focus actuator/driver, flex, RF preamp, optical Z-height or clamp
geometry) is somewhat more likely: many optical mechanisms require a valid
focus/reflection result before normal spin is authorized. A spindle
motor/driver/FG-feedback failure remains a strong alternative and can produce
the same externally visible sequence if the firmware requests spin but sees no
motion.

Decisive hardware checks
------------------------
1. During the first 0-2 s after LOAD, probe the spindle-motor outputs/current
   and FG/Hall feedback. Drive PWM/voltage with no rotation or FG points to the
   spindle motor, driver, feedback or mechanical drag; no drive request points
   upstream toward focus/RF qualification.
2. At the same time observe the focus-actuator waveform/S-curve, FE signal and
   RF envelope at the service test points. Repeated focus hunt without a valid
   S-curve/RF response implicates pickup/focus/Z-height rather than spindle.
3. With power disconnected, verify free spindle rotation, clamp seating and
   height/runout; inspect the pickup flex, connectors and solder joints, clean
   the lens, and check focus-coil continuity using service-manual limits.
4. Inspect spindle-driver supply rails and temperature/damage. If available,
   substitution with a known-good matching optical deck or PCB is the fastest
   split test. Direct independent LD/focus/spindle actuation would require a
   model-specific service mode or bench jig; no documented safe host CDB for
   the AD-5260S was found.

Bottom line: no software sequence changed the physical behavior. The strongest
new evidence is the repeatable internal 04/01 progress/deferred-operation trace
ending at 30/00 without medium-present. Focus/RF/focus-actuation is the leading
suspect, with spindle motor/driver/FG still a close, unresolved alternative.

################################################################################
# FINAL ROOT-LEVEL CONCLUSION (supersedes the earlier unprivileged reset note)
################################################################################

Completed UTC: 2026-08-27
Kernel: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic
Exact target: Optiarc DVD RW AD-5260S, firmware 1.00, SCSI 5:0:0:0,
              /dev/sr0 + /dev/sg3, libata ata6

Scope and persistence
---------------------
All privileged operations were gated by the exact vendor/model/HCTL identity.
No command was sent to sda, sdb, sdc, nvme0n1, their SCSI targets, or the shared
AHCI controller as a whole. No WRITE BUFFER, optical write, firmware flash,
EEPROM/NVRAM write, or other persistent drive modification was performed. The
kernel tracing and temporary dynamic-debug settings were restored; tracing is
off, selected events are disabled, and the target finishes in state=running.

The earlier conclusion said SG reset was blocked by missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN. That
was true only for the initial unprivileged pass. The following root-level tests
were subsequently completed and their raw logs/traces are appended below.

Concrete final media result
---------------------------
The pressed movie DVD behaves identically to the earlier known-good audio CD
and the other known-good media:

* Terminal TUR sense, byte-for-byte:
    70 00 02 00 00 00 00 0a 00 00 00 00 30 00 00 00 00 00
  Fixed current sense, key 02 NOT READY, ASC/ASCQ 30/00 INCOMPATIBLE MEDIUM
  INSTALLED. Host status is 0000 and driver transport status has no host error.
* GET CONFIGURATION is GOOD but current profile remains 0000. A full feature
  list is returned, showing that the command processor is alive; no active
  medium profile is selected.
* GET EVENT STATUS NOTIFICATION media returns:
    00 06 04 5e 00 00 00 00
  Door/tray closed, but firmware never asserts the media-present bit.
* READ CAPACITY(10), READ TOC, READ DISC INFORMATION, READ DVD STRUCTURE,
  READ(10), READ(12), and READ CD LBA 0 all finish promptly with the identical
  02/30/00 sense. Increasing TUR's host timeout from 5 s through 15 s to 60 s
  changes nothing; terminal replies take only about 17-24 ms.
* READ FORMAT CAPACITIES alone returns GOOD with a type-3 descriptor, i.e. no
  recognized medium. dvd+rw-mediainfo says "no media mounted"; cd-info cannot
  obtain the first track/TOC; UDisks reports Size=0 and no IdType.

Recognition state machine after real resets
-------------------------------------------
After each tray LOAD, the firmware still enters 02/04/01 BECOMING READY and
reports a repeatable SKSV progress sequence. The final root run observed:

* passive: maximum sampled 0x6666 (40.000%) at 1613.615 ms, collapse to 0x00da
  (0.333%) at 1802.803 ms, first 30/00 at 1911.997 ms;
* forced START/READ/F3 sequence: 0x6ccc (42.499%) at 1730.358 ms, 0x00da at
  1831.427 ms, first 30/00 at 1914.976 ms;
* synchronous LOAD returned GOOD after 1774.499 ms; first terminal 30/00 was
  sampled at 1897.918 ms.

These are the same stages and timing envelope as before administrator access.
START STOP UNIT (immediate/synchronous), low/max SET CD SPEED, READ requests,
and the audited NEC/Optiarc F3/01, F3/02, F3/03, F3/0f transient scan sequence
do not alter the curve. GESN status 3/Deferred counts down during this interval,
but media-present stays zero. Thus the firmware really runs an internal media
qualification sequence; it is not merely waiting on userspace.

Reset results
-------------
1. SG_SCSI_RESET_DEVICE and SG_SCSI_RESET_TARGET with --no-esc were attempted
   as root. The sg driver returned errno 5/EIO immediately for both; trace shows
   no reset action.
2. CDROMRESET ioctl returned success in 0.002 ms, but emitted no libata reset or
   link event and changed no sense/status. It is not a physical drive reset on
   this path. hdparm -w was rejected with ENOTTY. Exact sysfs rescan alone also
   changed nothing.
3. Deleting exactly SCSI 5:0:0:0 and reprobeing exactly host5 channel 0 target
   0 LUN 0 caused a genuine ata6-only recovery: hardreset (rc=-11/EAGAIN), then
   softreset (rc=0), IDENTIFY PACKET DEVICE, SET FEATURES and UDMA/100 setup.
   The drive was reattached as sr0/sg3 and identified correctly. Its very first
   TUR was still 02/30/00, current profile 0000, media-present zero, and the
   subsequent full recognition timeline remained unchanged.
4. An exploratory ATA PASS-THROUGH(16) used DEVICE RESET opcode 08h with the
   generic non-data protocol. It issued ATA_CMD_DEV_RESET, did not complete for
   30.331 s, and deliberately exercised kernel recovery: the command returned
   0b/00/00 ABORTED COMMAND after ata6 hardreset+softreset. SAT specifies a
   separate protocol value 9 for DEVICE RESET, so this protocol-mismatched
   timeout is not treated as evidence of an additional drive fault. It did,
   however, produce a second real port recovery, and media behavior again did
   not change.
5. Correctly encoded SAT protocol 9 DEVICE RESET, protocol 1 SRST, and protocol
   0 SATA COMRESET were each rejected locally by this libata SAT layer in about
   0.02 ms with 05/24/00 INVALID FIELD IN CDB. Trace shows SCSI start/done but
   no ata_qc_issue and no reset; these requests never reached the hardware.

Kernel trace and SATA interpretation
------------------------------------
Ordinary ATAPI CHECK CONDITIONs generate ata_qc_complete_failed followed by an
internal REQUEST SENSE. Linux libata schedules that sense path using
blk_abort_request(), which immediately invokes the SCSI timeout callback. That
is why trace_scsi_dispatch_cmd_timeout and sysfs iotmo_cnt rise even though the
commands finish in roughly 10-30 ms. In the ordinary load trace there were 170
such trace events and zero hardreset/softreset/freeze/thaw events. They are not
170 elapsed command timeouts. The only genuine ~30 s timeout in this work was
the explicitly protocol-mismatched ATA DEVICE RESET experiment described above.

The SATA PHY log ends with two deliberate PHYRDY->PHYRDYn transitions and three
COMRESET signatures (one pre-existing plus the two recovery cycles). Every
specific CRC and R_ERR counter remains zero. The PHY counter whose generic text
says "Command failed and ICRC error bit set" rises with ordinary ATAPI CHECK
CONDITIONs on this packet device; it does not correlate with CRC/R_ERR or link
resets and is not evidence of a bad SATA cable. INQUIRY/ATA IDENTIFY remain
coherent, the link is stable at 1.5 Gbit/s, and all final SCSI requests are
accounted for as completed.

What the software can and cannot split
--------------------------------------
The fault is below MMC/media recognition but above neither SATA nor the main
command MCU. Working elements include SATA transport, ATA/ATAPI command and
sense handling, firmware state machine, tray motor/sensors, pickup translation,
laser activation, identity/configuration memory, and at least part of the servo
control logic. The firmware never exposes 09/02 FOCUS SERVO FAILURE or 09/03
SPINDLE SERVO FAILURE; it collapses the terminal failure to 30/00. No host CDB,
reset, timeout, or known audited Optiarc scan command exposes spindle PWM/FG,
focus-lock/FOK, focus error, RF envelope, or laser-current telemetry. Therefore
software alone cannot conclusively choose spindle versus focus/RF.

Most probable culprit
----------------------
Given the invariant physical fact that neither known-good CD nor pressed DVD
ever starts rotating, the spindle path is now the leading single component
class: spindle motor/bearing, motor-driver/commutation stage, its supply, or
FG/back-EMF feedback. A common focus-acquisition/RF problem remains a close
second, because firmware may require a valid reflection/focus result before it
authorizes sustained spin. Identical failure on both CD and DVD makes a failure
of only one wavelength-specific laser diode less likely; it does not exclude
the common pickup optics, focus actuator/driver, flex cable, RF front end, or
mechanical optical height.

Decisive hardware split
-----------------------
During the first 0-2 s after LOAD, observe the spindle-driver command and phase
outputs/current together with FG/back-EMF feedback:

* commutation/drive present, no rotation and no FG -> spindle motor, bearing,
  clamp/drag, driver output stage, motor rail, or feedback path;
* no spindle-drive request -> inspect the upstream qualification gate: focus
  actuator waveform/S-curve, FE/FOK, photodiode/RF envelope, both laser paths,
  pickup flex/connectors, RF preamplifier, and optical Z-height;
* drive present and FG present but firmware still reports 30/00 -> examine
  speed/FG scaling and RF/focus acquisition under rotation.

With power disconnected, first confirm free spindle rotation and correct clamp
height/seating, check motor and focus-coil continuity against a service-manual
or known-good mechanism, inspect connector/flex soldering, and verify the motor
driver's relevant rails. A known-good matching optical deck/PCB split test is
the fastest confirmation, while preserving any board-specific calibration.
Firmware flashing is not indicated by these results and was not attempted.

Primary implementation/standard references used for interpretation
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Linux v6.8 libata core/EH and SCSI EH sources:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.8/drivers/ata/libata-core.c
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.8/drivers/ata/libata-eh.c
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.8/drivers/ata/libata-scsi.c
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/scsi/scsi_error.c
T10 SAT ATA PASS-THROUGH protocol clarification:
https://www.t10.org/ftp/t10/document.06/06-291r1.pdf
T10 MMC project page:
https://www.t10.org/members/w_mmc4.htm

Bottom line
-----------
Administrator access enabled genuine ata6 recovery and full kernel/libata
tracing, but neither changed a single media-visible result. The strongest new
evidence is negative: the drive survives re-identification and two real reset
recoveries with a clean SATA link, then reproduces the same internal 0->42.5%
->0.33%->30/00 path. This is a hardware servo/mechanism fault. Spindle/driver/
FG is the current leading suspect; common focus/pickup/RF remains the only
serious alternative until the two signals are measured at the mechanism.
